'''John (Jean) Iliopoulos''' ([[Greek language|Greek]]: Ιωάννης Ηλιόπουλος; 1940) is a [[Greeks|Greek]] [[physicist]]. He is the first person to present the [[Standard Model]] of [[particle physics]] in a single report.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Veltman |first=Martinus J. G. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xWdhDwAAQBAJ&pg=PT399 |title=Facts And Mysteries In Elementary Particle Physics |date=2018-03-21 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-323-707-0 |pages=399 |edition=Revised |language=en}}</ref> He is best known for his prediction of the [[charm quark]] with [[Sheldon Glashow]] and [[Luciano Maiani]] (the "[[Standard Model (mathematical formulation)#The GIM mechanism and the CKM matrix|GIM mechanism]]").<ref>{{cite journal |author1=S. L. Glashow |author2=J. Iliopoulos |author3=L. Maiani |journal=Phys. Rev.|volume=D2|pages=1285|year=1970|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.2.1285|bibcode = 1970PhRvD...2.1285G|title=Weak Interactions with Lepton-Hadron Symmetry|issue=7}}</ref> Iliopoulos is also known for demonstrating the cancellation of [[Anomaly (physics)|anomalies]] in the Standard model.<ref>Bouchiat, Cl,  Iliopoulos, J, and  Meyer, Ph (1972) . "An anomaly-free version of Weinberg's model." ''Physics Letters'' '''B38''', no. 7 (1972) 519-523.</ref> He is further known for the [[Fayet–Iliopoulos D-term]] formula, which was introduced in 1974.  He is currently an honorary member of Laboratory of [[theoretical physics]] of [[École Normale Supérieure|École normale supérieure]], Paris.

==Biography==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=February 2021}}
Iliopoulos graduated from [[National Technical University of Athens]] (NTUA) in 1962 as a Mechanical-Electrical Engineer.  He continued his studies in the field of Theoretical Physics in [[University of Paris]], and in 1963 he obtained the D.E.A, in 1965 the Doctorat 3e Cycle, and in 1968 the Doctorat d' Etat titles. Between the years 1966 and 1968 he was a scholar at [[CERN]], Geneva. From 1969 till 1971 he was a Research Associate in [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Hoddeson |first1=Lillian |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=klLUs2XUmOkC&pg=PA447 |title=The Rise of the Standard Model: A History of Particle Physics from 1964 to 1979 |last2=Brown |first2=Laurie |last3=Riordan |first3=Michael |last4=Dresden |first4=Max |date=1997-11-13 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-57816-5 |pages=447 |language=en}}</ref> In 1971 he returned in Paris and began working at [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]]. He also held the director position of the Laboratory of Theoretical Physics of the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] between the years 1991-1995 and 1998-2002. In 2002, Iliopoulos was the first recipient of the Aristeio prize, which has been instituted to recognize Greeks who have made significant contributions towards furthering their chosen fields of science. Iliopoulos and Maiani were jointly awarded the 1987 [[Sakurai Prize]] for theoretical particle physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prize Recipient |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm |access-date=2024-03-27 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2007 Iliopoulos and Maiani received the [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal of the ICTP]] "(f)or their work on the physics of the charm quark, a major contribution to the birth of the Standard Model, the modern theory of Elementary Particles." And in 2011, Glashow, Iliopoulos, and Maiani received the [[High Energy and Particle Physics Prize]], awarded by the [[European Physical Society|European Physical Society (EPS)]], "(f)or their crucial contribution to the theory of flavour, presently embedded in the Standard Theory of strong and electroweak interactions."<ref>{{Cite web |title=High Energy Particle Physics Board |url=https://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/eps-hepp/hepp-prize-awards.php |access-date=2024-03-27 |website=eps-hepp.web.cern.ch |archive-date=2020-08-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200818133406/http://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/eps-hepp/hepp-prize-awards.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
Iliopoulos is a specialist in high energy theoretical physics and elementary particle physics. In 1970, in collaboration with [[Sheldon Glashow]] and [[Luciano Maiani|Luciano Maïani]], he introduced the so-called "[[GIM mechanism]]" (named after the three authors) which is an essential element of the theory of fundamental interactions known as the "[[Standard Model]] ".<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Glashow|first1=S. L.|last2=Iliopoulos|first2=J.|last3=Maiani|first3=L.|date=1970-10-01|title=Weak Interactions with Lepton-Hadron Symmetry|journal=Physical Review D|publisher=American Physical Society (APS)|volume=2|issue=7|pages=1285–1292|doi=10.1103/physrevd.2.1285|bibcode=1970PhRvD...2.1285G |issn=0556-2821}}</ref> This mechanism postulates the existence of a new elementary particle, the "charmed" [[quark]], a prediction that was confirmed by experiments. In 1972, in collaboration with [[Claude Bouchiat]] and Philippe Meyer,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bouchiat|first1=C.|last2=Iliopoulos|first2=J.|last3=Meyer|first3=Ph.|year=1972|title=An anomaly-free version of Weinberg's model|journal=Physics Letters B|publisher=Elsevier BV|volume=38|issue=7|pages=519–523|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(72)90532-1|bibcode=1972PhLB...38..519B |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> he demonstrated that the mathematical coherence of the Standard Model requires symmetry between the elementary constituents of matter, namely quarks (which form [[hadron]]s such as [[proton]] and [[neutron]]) and [[lepton]]s (such as [[electron]], [[muon]] and [[neutrino]]s). This symmetry is also verified experimentally.

Iliopoulos was one of the pioneers of [[supersymmetry]], the hypothetical symmetry that links [[fermion]]s and [[boson]]s. He showed that it has remarkable convergence properties and, in collaboration with Pierre Fayet,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Fayet|first1=P.|last2=Iliopoulos|first2=J.|year=1974|title=Spontaneously broken supergauge symmetries and goldstone spinors|journal=Physics Letters B|publisher=Elsevier BV|volume=51|issue=5|pages=461–464|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(74)90310-4|bibcode=1974PhLB...51..461F |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> he proposed a mechanism that leads to its spontaneous breakage. He also studied some aspects of the [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]] of [[Gravity|gravitation]] as well as the mathematical properties of invariant [[Gauge theory|gauge theories]] formulated in a non-commutative geometric space.
